parsed.elsewhere_quote:
Consider a legal move on entries \(m,n>1\), and put \(g=\gcd(m,n)\). The product of the two new entries is
\[
g\cdot\frac{\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)}g
=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=\frac{mn}{g}.
\]
parsed.explanation: The quoted inference is false: a positive nonincreasing integer sequence may reach zero. However, the earlier product calculation supplies the missing argument. Since a legal move has m,n>1, lcm(m,n)>1, so the two outputs have product greater than 1 and cannot both be 1. Thus every move leaves at least one nonunit, while the termination argument and the terminal at-most-one argument are valid. Replacing the false sentence with this observation repairs the display.
